title: chunkio/memory_close.qcore supports the resource-v1 cio_chunk_close view only on memory-backed chunks
why: Card CONTRACT-VIEW-PROJECTION-CHECK checks every multi-module declaration as a registered relation (qcore_contract::contract_views). The relation memory_close.qcore -> resource_open_close.qcore holds only under the computed, pinned premise nonnull_chunk_has_memory_backend, classified Coverage: outside it the detailed contract says nothing about the chunk (Lean QCore.ContractViewProjection.outside_the_memory_backend_the_view_is_not_implied), while chunkio/resource_open_close.qcore's resource_released(chunk, nonnull) is applied by the resource loader to every call whatever the backend. The view is also entailed by chunkio/chunk_destructor.qcore on every backend, but that is a language-level lifecycle contract, not a source-checked one. The filesystem and unsupported-backend policies (filesystem_chunk_close.qcore, unsupported_close.qcore) declare other names and are not related to the view. Nothing moves a verdict: the view was already a trusted assumption. Discharge: a checked relation from a source-checked declaration of cio_chunk_close covering the other backends to the view, or a premise on the view that narrows it to what is supported.

title: The resource-v1 views are entailed only under detailed premises the v1 checker does not enforce
why: Card CONTRACT-VIEW-PROJECTION-CHECK computes, for each projection, which detailed requires clauses the view's own custody discipline discharges; the rest are pinned per relation with a class (Profile, Environment, Coverage). flb_malloc/flb_calloc/flb_free assume ordinary_allocator_profile == 1 (Profile, fixed for the audited build). chunk_destructor.qcore -> resource_open_close.qcore assumes chunk_is_not_busy and chunk_has_no_task_or_route_custody (Environment). memory_close.qcore -> resource_open_close.qcore assumes nine premises besides its Coverage one (seven Environment: disjoint owned provenance, live reciprocal and distinct link memberships, context/stream lifetime, counter coverage, no lock/busy/task/route/transaction obligations, exclusive access; two Profile: cross-unit source/ABI bindings, free resolving to libc). The v1 vocabulary has no clause for any of them, so every call site the view covers assumes them. Discharge: a v1 premise vocabulary the loader checks at call sites, or a per-premise argument that the pinned corpus establishes it.

title: chunkio/error_frame.qcore and chunkio/error_state.qcore are renamed equivalents kept as two views
why: Card CONTRACT-VIEW-PROJECTION-CHECK measured the two cio_error_reset declarations: token-equal under the four-word renaming Chunk->cio_chunk, chunk_is_live->object_is_live, exclusive_chunk_access->exclusive_object_access, lock_is_preserved->modeled_fields_are_preserved, and both real frame evaluators (evaluate_chunk_frame_contract, evaluate_boolean_frame_contract) accept exactly the same write vectors over a 31-summary family for both imported protected sets {lock} and {busy, lock}; the equivalence holds exactly when the protected set contains lock and excludes the written field error_n (Lean QCore.ContractViewProjection.the_frame_evaluators_agree_under_the_condition, the_condition_is_load_bearing). They are not deleted: each is the pinned contract of a different evaluator flavour (qcore_verification::frame_source::FrameContractFlavour), bound by digest into its frame-helper task identity, and the Chunk flavour is also bundled by compiler/src/verifier_plugins/chunkio/memory_close.rs and the retained Cycle 19 adapters; an evaluator refuses the other vocabulary by design, and retiring the Chunk flavour's contract is a route change under invariant 3. Discharge: retire the Chunk flavour's own contract with archived parity, or give it a checked renaming input from error_frame.qcore, then delete error_state.qcore's declaration.

title: The view-entailment decision procedure's exactness is argued, not proved in Lean
why: qcore_contract::contract_views::entails decides entailment over the equality fragment (literals, ghost names, ==, !=, and, or, not) by enumerating each name over the involved literals, 0 and 1, plus fresh values sized by the largest group of directly compared names, after restricting premises to the goal's cone of influence. Its exactness rests on a small-model argument documented in the Rust module; the Lean model (QCore.ContractViewProjection) proves each registered entailment directly over the integers and that dropping premises is sound, but not the enumeration lemma itself, and the fragment evaluator's parity with the shared interpreter is a Rust test over a grid. Discharge: a Lean proof of the small-model lemma for the fragment, or an extraction of the Rust enumerator.

title: The bridges from detailed vocabularies to resource-v1 predicates are declared translations
why: Card CONTRACT-VIEW-PROJECTION-CHECK checks a projection through a declared bridge per detailed vocabulary (ALLOCATOR_OBSERVATION_BRIDGE, CHUNK_CLOSE_MECHANISM_BRIDGE, CHUNK_CLOSE_LANGUAGE_BRIDGE): for example resource_return_owned(nullable) means (result_null == 1 and live_after == 0) or (result_null == 0 and live_after == 1 and result_is_backend == 1); v1 nullable custody of flb_free's argument is identified with valid_input_extent == 1 (null or a live allocation of the same allocator, so the allocator-family match is part of the identification); result_null is 0/1 by the native adapter; chunk release is chunk_released (memory_close) or chunk_name_and_object_are_released with a consumed own<Chunk> (chunk_destructor). These identifications are premises of every projection check, stated in code and in the report, not derived from the resource checker's semantics. Discharge: a Lean or Rust statement of the v1 custody semantics from which each bridge rule follows.

title: The retained Cycle 18 timeout-teardown evidence binds the pre-card timeout policy digest
why: Card CONTRACT-VIEW-PROJECTION-CHECK removed monkey/timeout_teardown.qcore's source_identity declaration, a textual duplicate of monkey/wait_source_policy.qcore's; qcore_verification::timeout_teardown now evaluates the owner's declaration and binds its SHA-256 as source_identity_digest in the projection and in TimeoutTeardownEvidence. The timeout policy's own digest therefore moves (516fa1fe... -> the card's), and the retained native evidence in docs/reports/cycle18-priority1-integration/ (timeout-report.json) records the old one. The workspace tests that derive evidence from the projection pass; no native quirin-audit timeout-teardown or cycle18-composition run was made by this card. Discharge: rerun the configured timeout-teardown and Cycle 18 composition audits natively against the canonical files and publish the new digests beside the frozen report.
